sources.title: AIPRM prompts page: Human Written |100% Unique |SEO Optimised Article

source_inspiration.outside_user_need: Huge usage around article/SEO writing help signals demand for writing assistance and publish-ready article workflows.
source_inspiration.pathforge_fit_adaptation: The idea was altered into an offline Source Citation Freshness Flipbook where a writer pastes claims/sources, marks source age and evidence type, sees deterministic freshness warnings, flips through risky citations, and copies an editor handoff. It does not generate article text, perform SEO automation, call web search, or wrap a hosted AI/API.
source_inspiration.offline_reason: PathForge should be able to serve and verify the result without live search, hosted AI calls, remote fonts, CDN scripts/styles, external APIs, or fragile remote dependencies.
source_inspiration.no_copy_statement: No third-party prompt text was copied; the AIPRM metrics were treated as market research only.

steps.prompt_exact: I’m editing research-heavy articles and want a self-contained desktop/tablet HTML flipbook where I can paste a handful of claims with source notes, mark each source’s age and evidence type, get freshness warnings, flip through the riskiest citations, and copy a clean editor handoff without doing live web lookup.
steps.response_summary: Qwen3.7 Plus produced a self-contained citation freshness flipbook HTML file with source age/evidence scoring, tabs, export, and local storage, but the code used inline handlers and dynamic HTML rendering.
code_blocks:
📚 Research Claim Flipbook

Paste claims, tag evidence, assess freshness risk, and generate clean editor handoffs. 100% offline.

How Risk is Calculated: Total Risk Score $R = A + E$, where $A$ is the Age Penalty ($0$ if $\le 2$ years, $+1$ if $2-5$ years, $+2$ if $>5$ years) and $E$ is the Evidence Penalty (Meta-analysis $= 0$, RCT $= 1$, Observational $= 2$, Expert $= 3$, Anecdotal $= 4$). Risk levels: $R \le 1$ (Low), $2 \le R \le 3$ (Medium), $R \ge 4$ (High).
0 / 0

This generates a clean, structured Markdown-ready handoff for your editorial CMS or team.

Copied successfully!
steps.notes: V1 was not accepted because static inspection found inline onclick/onchange handlers, dynamic innerHTML template rendering for user content, alert/confirm modal APIs, and scanner-visible unsafe sinks.

steps.prompt_exact: This is close, but the generated HTML uses inline onclick handlers and injects claim/source text through string-built markup, which is risky for pasted notes and would fail my review gate. Please rewrite it as a complete self-contained HTML file with addEventListener controls and DOM/textContent rendering for all user-entered content, keeping the same citation freshness flipbook and editor handoff workflow.
steps.response_summary: Qwen3.7 Plus rewrote the tool with addEventListener controls and textContent/createElement rendering for user-entered content, but the repaired code still had scanner-visible innerHTML clearing and alert/confirm modal APIs.
